abstract: We have examined the effects of dietary retinoids upon the growth and differentiation of seven embryonal carcinoma lines in mice. The control diet contained 4000 IU/mg retinyl palmitate; the other diets contained 2 x 10(5) IU/mg retinyl palmitate, 50 mg/kg all-trans-retinoic acid (RA), 100 mg/kg RA, and no retinoid. The RA-containing diets had little influence on tumor latency or incidence but did suppress growth of many of the tumors. Decreased tumor mass was, in most but not all instances, accompanied by an increased proportion of differentiated cells. Increased differentiation was most commonly quantitative rather than qualitative; i.e., there was a larger proportion of the same types of differentiated cells seen in tumors from the control diet group rather than an increase in the spectrum of cell types observed. Notably, tumors from two differentiation-defective embryonal carcinoma lines were refractory to both the differentiation-inducing and growth-suppressing properties of dietary RA. Taken together, our results suggest that dietary RA can reduce teratocarcinoma growth in part by promoting differentiation but that other mechanisms are likely to be involved. The therapeutic benefits that we observed with dietary RA were compromised by adverse effects, including failure of the mice to gain weight as effectively as those on the control diet. The effects of elevated levels of retinyl palmitate, or its omission from the diet, were much less striking than that of RA. Both modifications tended to decrease tumor latency but had little effect, if any, upon ultimate tumor mass. Elimination of retinoid from the diet failed to significantly reduce degree of differentiation in tumors which normally differentiate extensively in animals on retinoid-containing diets. Excess retinyl palmitate led to a marginal increase in differentiation in F9 tumors and a statistically significant increase in differentiation in OC15-S1 tumors. Tumors from other embryonal carcinoma lines did not contain elevated levels of differentiated cells. The interpretation of these results is complicated by our observations that although our dietary alteration in levels of palmitate were dramatic, they resulted in much more modest differences in circulating retinoid levels when compared with mice on the control diet.
abstract_ja: 7種類のマウス胎児性癌細胞株由来の腫瘍について、食事性レチノイドが増殖と分化に及ぼす影響を検討した。対照食は4000 IU/mgのパルミチン酸レチニルを含み、他の食餌は2×10^5 IU/mgのパルミチン酸レチニル、50 mg/kgおよび100 mg/kgの全トランスレチノイン酸(RA)、またはレチノイドを含まないものであった。RA含有食は腫瘍の潜伏期や発生率にはほとんど影響しなかったが、多くの腫瘍の増殖を抑制した。腫瘍質量の減少は、ほとんどの場合、分化細胞の割合の増加を伴ったが、例外もあった。分化の増加は、主に量的なものであり、すなわち観察される分化細胞の種類の範囲が広がるよりも、対照食群の腫瘍で見られる同じ種類の分化細胞の割合が多かった。特に、分化欠陥型の2株の胎児性癌由来腫瘍は、RAによる分化誘導作用と増殖抑制作用の両方に抵抗性を示した。以上の結果から、食事性RAは分化促進を一部介して奇形癌の増殖を抑制しうるが、他の機序も関与していると考えられる。RAによる治療効果は、マウスの体重増加が対照食群より低下するという有害作用により損なわれた。パルミチン酸レチニルの増減の影響は、RAの影響に比べてはるかに小さかった。両修飾は腫瘍潜伏期を短縮する傾向にあったが、最終的な腫瘍質量にはほとんど影響しなかった。食からレチノイドを除去しても、通常は食餌中のレチノイドにより広範に分化する腫瘍での分化度は有意に低下しなかった。パルミチン酸レチニルの過剰は、F9腫瘍でわずかな分化増加、OC15-S1腫瘍で統計的に有意な分化増加をもたらした。他の胎児性癌株の腫瘍では分化細胞の増加は見られなかった。これらの結果の解釈は、食餌中のパルミチン酸レチニル量の変化が大きくても、循環中のレチノイド濃度の差は対照食群と比べてはるかに小さいという観察により複雑である。
